text: A bamboo flute drifts through the green: a slow tune you almost recognize. Your heart settles, and a thread of qi gathers without your asking.
A seedpod the color of old gold drops into your sleeve. It is heavier than it should be — tomorrow's tea or tonight's pillow, you cannot tell.
Beneath the water, something flashes silver — a sword's hilt, or a fish's belly. It is gone before you can be sure.
A child bumps into your hip. By the time you turn, three spirit stones are missing and the child is laughing two stalls away.

Down the side-alley behind the cloth-stall, a shop-front has been sealed with a strip of fresh paper. A woman sits on the step with her hands folded; her husband has been ill nine days, a neighbour mutters, and no Azure Cloud healer has come. She raises her eyes at you, weighs the weigh, and looks away. Someone has already failed her once.
Somewhere in the hills a voice cries out — abruptly, and then is silent. The crows do not even bother to look up.
White petals fall from no tree you can see. They melt against your face like snow, and leave a strange clarity behind.
Lantern-light catches a column of dust drifting through the scrolls. For one heartbeat, the motes seem to spell a word — then they are only dust again.
